days.title: Hike over Aasgard Pass to Gnome Tarn

days.title: Climb the finger crack and Stanley-Burgner

days.note: The 80 ft 5.10+ finger crack starts about 20 ft left of the normal Stanley-Burgner start and tops out at the same belay, so most parties link it into Stanley-Burgner P2 and continue to the summit. days.title: Hike out via the Snow Lakes

days.note: The Snow Lakes trail is about 10 mi from the Prusik area and loses more than a mile of elevation; reports run from about 4 hours (light) to about 6 hours (loaded) from the base of Prusik to the car. This needs a car or shuttle at the Snow Lakes trailhead; reversing Aasgard Pass is the alternative.

days.title: Climb the West Ridge

days.note: The classic, easiest technical route on Prusik -- moving parties often simulclimb the low-5th-class ridge in about 90 minutes. Descend by rappelling the north side and walking back over Prusik Pass, leaving the afternoon free to explore the basin.

days.objective: Return to the Stuart Lake trailhead
days.note: Break camp, climb back up to Aasgard Pass, then descend the long way back past Colchuck Lake to the trailhead. Efficient parties sometimes skip this third day and hike all the way out the same evening after climbing, making it a 2-day trip.

camps_on_file.name: Inspiration and Perfection Lakes

days.title: Approach to treeline bivy

days.title: Climb Vanishing Point
days.objective: Climb all 14 pitches
days.note: Climb the full 14-pitch route, a very long day given the sustained 5.10-5.12 climbing with few easy pitches.

days.title: Walk off to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Barclay Lake trailhead
days.note: Descend via the roughly 3-hour descent route back to the trailhead, or do this the same day if fast.

camps_on_file.name: Dolomite Tower bivy caves
camps_on_file.notes: Shallow caves about 150 ft right of the start of the route. Spray can blow in during wind and rain.
